evidence.claim: External tree scan report: both Music and Videos are full checkouts; three real finds (stricter semantic-entity contract, T.I.E. link hardening, four genuinely missing modules), one trap (external T.I.E. reads a different store), and no successor authority in either tree.
Pre-change contract ACCEPTED an identity with the qualifier omitted; the replacement refuses it, closing an unauditable-identity hole.
Before hardening, a symlinked experience log was read as genuine subject history (red). After adding reject_path_links it is reported corrupt_or_unavailable with no records (green).
110 passed across tie fusion, usage memory, model-group preparation, entity contract, secure publish and contract length after both changes.

learned: External scan: Music and Videos are both full checkouts (Music nests one level deeper, which my first scan misread as absence). Three real finds acted on: the Videos semantic-entity contract requires qualifier and is stricter than mine (mine permitted an unauditable identity; now replaced, proved against the preserved pre-change copy); T.I.E. link rejection ported (red/green); four genuinely missing modules identified as portable. One trap avoided: the external fuse reads .engineering-bootstrap/studios revisions while our recorder writes orchestration/workflows/.../memory, so adopting it wholesale would make every fusion report corrupt_or_unavailable; also its binding requires version, which ours does not. Two of my own analysis errors were corrected mid-work: the Music-root scan path and my claim that a malformed qualifier was the divergence (it legitimately matches the pattern; the real divergence is a missing qualifier).
